text.p: French hotel group Accor SA is expected to report a rise in 1996 profit, boosted by gains from the sale of shares in Compass Plc and the sale and leaseback of hotels, analysts say.

The consensus estimate for Accor's 1996 net attributable profit compiled by Paris-based consultant Jacques Chahine Finance is for 1.05 billion francs, compared with net attributable profit of 923 million francs for the preceding year. Estimates range from 1.0 to 1.23 billion francs.
Accor is scheduled to report its 1996 results on April 23 after the stockmarket's close at 1500 GMT.

One analyst, who expects net attributable profit of 1.03 billion francs, said he expected 550 million francs, or more than half, to come from exceptional gains -- around 300 million from the sale and leaseback of hotels and 250 million from the sale of Compass shares.
Accor said last month that it had reduced its stake in Compass to 10 percent after placing 11.5 percent with institutional investors. It sold 1.9 percent in December.

Last April co-chairmen Gerard Pelisson and Paul Dubrule forecast that the group, which runs the Ibis, Sofitel, Mercure, Novotel and U.S.-based Motel 6 chains, would report higher net attributable and operating profits for 1996.

Accor said in October when it published first-half results that it expected to show an operating profit of 1.5 billion francs for 1996, up 220 million francs. It also announced the appointment of a new management board chairman, Jean-Marc Espalioux.
In January it reported its 50-50 Europcar venture with Volkswagen showed an operating profit for 1996.
